chunks: Surely your Lord is God who created the heavens and the earth in six spans of time, then assumed all power. He covers up the day with night which comes chasing it fast; and the sun and moon and the stars are subject to His command. It is His to create and enjoin. Blessed be God, the Lord of all the worlds.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's creation of the heavens and earth and His authority over the cosmos?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is pivotal for establishing Tawhid al-Rabbaniyyah (Divine Lordship), where 'Al-Arsh' (Throne) is often interpreted not merely as a physical seat but as the locus of divine authority and the highest level of creation. The phrase 'Yastawī 'ala al-'Arsh' highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty, while the subservience of celestial bodies underscores the unity of creation and command (Al-Khalq wa al-Amr), a concept frequently linked to the Imams' role as the manifest signs of this divine order.
